title: Estate Buyer's Desk Note on Outright Purchase and Consignment
content:
Under the estate programme of the Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes the chain buys the piece outright or offers it on consignment, and the customer chooses which of the two before the piece is taken in. The choice between credit, an outright purchase and consignment is made by the customer on the trade-in service request record, because disposing of their own property is theirs alone to do.

## Outright purchase

An outright purchase pays the programme's share of the appraised value and is settled in money rather than in credit, and the piece becomes the chain's on the day it is paid for. A piece bought in is held for the days the trade requires before it is resold or melted, whatever the customer or a buyer asks for in the meantime.

## Consignment

A consigned piece is offered for the programme's consignment period and the chain retains its commission out of the price achieved; a piece that does not sell is returned to the customer at the end of the period. A piece is taken on consignment only where its appraised value reaches the programme's consignment floor, and a piece below that floor is offered an outright purchase instead. The consignment commission is retained out of the price the piece achieves rather than charged to the customer, and the valuation entry records the basis the price was struck on.

Whether outright purchase is offered, the share of the appraised value it pays, the commission, the consignment period, the consignment floor, the metal holding period and the scrap rate are the programme's published figures.

## The choice in a table

| The customer chooses | What follows |
|---|---|
| credit | credit is issued under the programme |
| outright purchase | the programme's share of the appraised value is paid in money; the piece is the chain's from the day it is paid for and is held for the trade's holding period before resale or melting |
| consignment, appraised value at or above the floor | the piece is offered for the consignment period; the commission comes out of the price achieved; an unsold piece goes back to the customer at the end of the period |
| consignment, appraised value below the floor | an outright purchase is offered instead |

## Hypothetical case

A piece appraised below the programme's consignment floor is brought in by a customer who asks for consignment. The desk offers an outright purchase instead; if the customer accepts, the programme's share of the appraised value is paid in money and the piece is held for the trade's holding period before it is resold or melted, however soon a buyer asks for it.
